authorization_deviation.what: One request was sent to the account-level endpoint GET /reminders/lists at 2026-11-11T01:55:19Z, after the window had closed and the gate had been verified closed.
authorization_deviation.how: The step after the window was meant to be an independent read-only recheck, and it used the client's `gate` subcommand. That subcommand is R1-only: it targets /reminders/lists. R1-03 forbids that endpoint on every path, including the ones that change nothing.
authorization_deviation.why_it_was_wrong: The subcommand is documented in the client's own header as deprecated for R1-03, and the correct closed-gate recheck is a `probe --phase post`, which the window had already done. Choosing `gate` was a mistake in the recheck step, not a gap in the tooling.
authorization_deviation.what_it_returned: HTTP 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with no list metadata in the body. The gate was closed at that moment, so the request was refused before any list was produced.
authorization_deviation.what_is_claimed: That the request was sent and was refused with 403. That is the whole claim.
authorization_deviation.what_is_not_claimed: Not claimed: that nothing was enumerated underneath. A 403 at the entry gate is not a measurement of what EventKit did internally, and this receipt does not use it as one.
authorization_deviation.corrective_rule_from_now_on: Every closed-gate recheck, manual or automatic, goes through `probe --phase post` on the item endpoint - the same request class the window itself uses. The `gate` subcommand is not used in any R1-03 path again. This rule is also recorded in section 7.4.4 of the application.

what_this_does_not_prove: It does not prove the list was deleted, that it left the account, or that the account changed. Only that the identifier does not resolve in this store at this time.
It does not distinguish a deleted list from a list that was never synced to this Mac, from a source-scope change, or from a list sitting in Recently Deleted.
It does not show that EventKit enumerated nothing underneath; the allowlist rejects at the entry gate, before calendar(withIdentifier:).

The 404 is produced by the deployed binary; the Swift-side handling of a missing identifier is covered by source reading, not by an independent end-to-end test (that gap is registered in section 4.4 of the application).
verdict_assertion: The bound list 9D9A****03F3 does not resolve on MAC-1 as of 2026-11-11T01:54:46Z. With the gate open and the store healthy, GET /reminders/lists/9D9A****03F3/items returned HTTP 404 LIST_NOT_FOUND; the same request before the gate opened and after it closed returned 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, so the 404 is an answer from an open gate, not a refusal. Combined with R1's enumeration result (two lists, target absent) this says the identifier is gone from this store's view; it does not say why.
